_policy: ALLOWLIST, not an exclusion list. A path ships in a public release ONLY if it
matches one of the glob patterns in `allow` below. Anything unmatched is
excluded by default — this is the whole point: unlisted means blocked, always,
fails closed by construction rather than by remembering to deny the right thing.
Enforced by ops/verify-public-release.mjs, which scans the ASSEMBLED PUBLISH
CANDIDATE directory (the tree that would actually be pushed/mirrored), not the
private source tree. Every allow/neverAllow pattern here is a path relative to
that candidate's root.
There is no --force, no skip flag, no env-var bypass in the verify script.
The only way to change what ships is to edit THIS file, in a normal reviewed
diff — so the decision is visible to whoever reviews it, not buried in a flag
someone passed once under deadline pressure. Two scan layers get their OWN
reviewed-exception mechanism, same discipline, different file because their
findings aren't path-shaped: gitleaks findings are suppressed only via
ops/public-release-gitleaks-baseline.json (gitleaks' own --baseline-path — a
known industry mechanism, not reinvented here). Verified empirically:
gitleaks' baseline matcher compares nearly the WHOLE finding record — RuleID,
File, StartLine/EndLine, StartColumn/EndColumn, Entropy — not just its
Fingerprint field, so an entry must be the finding's own object copied from a
real report, never hand-typed. This manifest's own `reviewedContentFindings`
array below suppresses the custom PII/production-id-shape grep instead, keyed
by a `path:pattern:hash` fingerprint (a sha256 hash of the literal matched text,
truncated to 16 hex chars — never the value itself, so a suppression entry
never has to contain the sensitive value it's suppressing). Deliberately NOT
keyed by line number (2026-09-10 fix): a line-numbered key is fail-open by
construction — line numbers shift on any edit above them, so a stale entry
silently suppresses WHATEVER new match lands on that old line, not the specific
value it was reviewed for. Hashing the matched text instead means a shifted line
with a different value produces a different key and correctly surfaces as
unreviewed; the same literal recurring anywhere else in the same file, at any
line, still suppresses — deliberate, since identical matched text is the
identical reviewed fact regardless of which line it sits on. Both start empty.
A file the verifier skips for being oversized (over 2MB text / 25MB binary) FAILS
the gate by default (2026-09-10 fix) -- gitleaks hunts credentials, not PII, so an
unscanned file is not a covered file just because it passed the path allowlist. The
only way to ship one anyway is `oversizedExceptions` below, keyed the same way as
reviewedContentFindings (2026-09-13 fix): path:sha256(content).slice(0,16), not path
alone -- exact-path-only keying was fail-open on replacement, since a later release
could swap a different, larger, sensitive file into an already-approved path with no
re-review and no signal (the identical fail-open shape this manifest's own
reviewedContentFindings scheme eliminated from line-numbered fingerprints, one level
up -- from "line" to "file"). For a human who has actually read the file's content
and is willing to say so in the reason. Starts empty, same as the other two exception
lists.
Directories that accumulate operational runbooks, benchmark fixtures, or
reference docs (ops/, benchmarks/, muse-brain/docs/) are allowlisted FILE BY
FILE, not by a directory glob — that is deliberate. A `benchmarks/**`, `ops/**`,
or `docs/**` glob would auto-admit the next unreviewed fixture, runbook, or
image dropped into any of them, which is exactly the failure this manifest
exists to prevent (see benchmarks/golden/ below, and muse-brain/docs/images/
banner.png's shipped-with-a-real-legal-name-in-its-metadata incident — a
`docs/**` glob was the pattern that let that ship, caught only by a 2026-09
audit, not by this manifest).
Code trees with no history of fixture-shaped subdirectories (src/, migrations/,
cli/, runner/) are allowlisted by directory glob, since there is nothing in
their shape for a stray real-data fixture to hide inside.
Built by reading what public v1.10.0 (falcoschaefer99-eng/muse-brain, tag
a5a98ae7, == public/main HEAD as of this manifest's creation) actually shipped —
fetched into refs/pubtags/* to avoid colliding with this repo's own same-named
private v1.10.0 tag (1048352a), which points to a different commit entirely.
_howToInvoke: Publishing is currently a MANUAL process — no automated mirror/release script
exists in this repo yet. Until one does, run this by hand as the last step
before pushing anything to the public remote. THREE steps, not two — the
middle one is not optional. verify-public-release.mjs only SCANS a candidate;
it never assembles or filters one. Feeding it a raw `git archive | tar -x`
tree hands it the entire tracked source tree, unfiltered, which contains many
paths this manifest has never allowlisted — the gate then correctly FAILS on
every one of them (findUnlistedPaths -> failed = true). That is not a bug in
the gate; it is what "unlisted means blocked" means. The missing middle step
was itself a real defect (found 2026-09, fixed the same day this note was
written): following the previous two-step version of these instructions
exactly could never reach a passing gate.
1. Export the ref's tracked working tree to a scratch directory:
git archive <ref> | tar -x -C /path/to/source
2. Assemble a candidate containing ONLY allowlisted paths, from the
muse-brain/ package directory:
node ../ops/assemble-public-release.mjs /path/to/source /path/to/candidate
(add --force if /path/to/candidate already exists and should be wiped
and rebuilt fresh rather than erroring on a non-empty directory)
3. Run the gate against the ASSEMBLED candidate, not the raw source tree:
npm run verify-public-release -- /path/to/candidate
(or directly: node ../ops/verify-public-release.mjs /path/to/candidate)
Only proceed to mirror/push to the public remote once the gate exits 0 -- not a
fourth build step, just the reminder this whole gate exists to enforce.
If a future release/mirror automation script is added, wire both steps 2 and 3
into it the same way `predeploy` gates `npm run deploy` today — as
unconditional prerequisite steps, not optional ones.

neverAllow.reason: Real-corpus-derived benchmark fixtures. A 2026-09 security audit found this directory staged for the pending v1.11.0 public release containing verbatim private conversations — financial hardship, welfare status, tax details, and a third party's name — about a living person. It has never been published (public v1.10.0 does not contain it either). Do not re-add without a fresh, explicit privacy review of every fixture inside it; excluding it from publication does not change what happens to it in the private repo, which is a separate, deliberately deferred decision.

Contains a real Neon Postgres pooler hostname and a real Cloudflare account ID in plaintext (as of this writing, roughly lines 46/52/55 — re-check before ever reconsidering this). Already correctly excluded from public v1.10.0; recorded here so that exclusion stops being tribal knowledge one person has to remember.

Falco's explicit call, 2026-09-08: 'do not under any circumstances ship with backfill receipts to new end users using muse brain, that is embarrassing.' Two independently sufficient grounds: (1) this is an internal operational artifact — one backfill run's own receipts — with zero consumer-facing value to a self-hoster; (2) its production observation IDs carry second-precision timestamps that reconstruct months of one real person's private-memory write cadence, a behavioral timeline about a living person, not a config example. This file DID ship in public v1.10.0 (its prior `allow` entry's own reason was 'Already shipped in public v1.10.0' — inertia, not review) — the historical exposure is known and already public; this entry only stops it from shipping again. The file itself is untouched and stays tracked in the private repo; this is a publication decision, not a deletion.
